name: Marisla Foundation Environment Program
summary: Foundation grants for marine and coastal biodiversity conservation in California, northwest Mexico, Hawaii, Chile and the Western Pacific. Tax-exempt organisations apply online in four annual windows, with no letter of inquiry.

geography.label: California, Northwest Mexico, Hawaii, Chile, and the Western Pacific (Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia)

eligibility.rule: Has tax-exempt status under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code
Does not support candidates for political office
No other application in the past 12 months, unless a fiscal sponsor of nonprofits

calls.label: Quarterly application windows
calls.recurring: Applications close at midnight Eastern on January 15, April 15, July 15 and October 15 each year.

status.quote: Applications may be submitted online only within the two-month windows detailed below in the Application Deadlines.

recurring.quote: The application must be submitted by midnight Eastern Standard Time (U.S.) or 9:00pm Pacific Standard Time (U.S.) on January 15, April 15, July 15 and October 15.

applicant_types.quote: The Foundation is able to support only those organizations that have received tax-exempt status under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code.

geography.quote: Primary emphasis is on marine and coastal biodiversity conservation with a geographic focus on California, Northwest Mexico, Hawaii, Chile, and the Western Pacific (Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia).

access.quote: the Foundation uses an online application system exclusively. We do not require or accept letters of inquiry (LOIs).

window.quote: The Marisla Foundation Board of Directors makes funding decisions on a quarterly basis.

eligibility.quote: The Foundation is able to support only those organizations that have received tax-exempt status under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code.
Grants are not made to individuals or for activities that support candidates for political office.
The Foundation also will not review more than one application per year (any twelve-month period) from any organization, with the exception of organizations that are fiscal sponsors of nonprofits.
